bullets.title: MRVL/LITE: Marvell acquires Lumentum for $115B in all-stock deal
bullets.body: Marvell confirmed acquisition of Lumentum at 4.5 MRVL shares per LITE share (~$1,132/share, 23.9% premium), implying $115B enterprise value; LITE shareholders to own ~33% of combined entity post-close. Deal targets >$1B annual run-rate cost synergies (primarily COGS), expected accretive to MRVL non-GAAP EPS in year one after close (expected H1 2028). Strategic rationale centers on optical interconnect leadership, CPO/scale-in optics, and a combined $550B+ TAM; Wolfe maintains MRVL Outperform at $375 PT while JPM notes valuation favors COHR (12x CY28) and FN (14x) over LITE (21x pre-deal).

bullets.title: AAPL: Reports today; JPM raises PT to $360, OPCO/OPCO cautious on valuation
bullets.body: JPM's Samík raised AAPL PT to $360 (from $340) citing a durable iPhone cycle with Duo demand still outstripping supply; F1Q27 guide expected at $147.9B revenue (+3% YoY). UBS models Sept-Q iPhone revenue ~$56B (+14% YoY, decelerating), total revenue $112.8B, EPS $1.97; Services App Store growing low-single-digits, ~800bps slower than year-ago. OPCO flags AAPL FY27 EPS ~7% below consensus on slowing iPhone growth and rising memory costs, with shares near a 15-year forward P/E peak.

bullets.title: ORCL: Files $10B equity + $10B debt offerings; Stephens upgrades to OW, $213 PT
bullets.body: Oracle filed a $10B common stock offering (424B5, stock at $130.67) and a $10B debt offering (424B2) simultaneously, sending shares down ~3% in pre-market. Stephens upgraded ORCL to Overweight from Equal-Weight, raising PT to $213 from $185 (63% upside), though the equity raise is dilutive near-term. Snowflake's launch as a native service on OCI is a positive for Oracle's cloud ecosystem.

bullets.title: ANET: JPM reiterates OW, $250 PT; pullback creates favorable setup into Q3 earnings
bullets.body: ANET is down 14% since 2Q earnings; JPM sees the pullback as a favorable entry ahead of 3Q results, modeling revenue $3.30B vs. consensus $3.33B. JPM expects ANET to guide ~30% 2027 revenue growth initially (path to 35%+), driven by hyperscaler capex growing 69% YoY in 2027 and a $2B+ AI Lab customer (via Broadcom TPU deployment). TAM expands to $340B+ by 2030 from $105B in 2025; PT $250 on 45x 2028E EPS.

bullets.title: PLTR: Channel checks strong; MS EW citing valuation; UBS bullish as best AI enabler
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley channel checks suggest PLTR Q3 revenues grew 92–94% YoY with a 5–6% beat vs. guidance, but analyst awaits a better entry at ~70x CY27 FCF. UBS characterizes PLTR as the best AI enabler in the market with US Commercial revenue +149% YoY in Q2 and 2027 FCF multiple of 51x, flagging sustainability of growth as comps materialize. MS maintains EW; UBS is constructive.

bullets.title: FOXA: Q1 record beat — revenue $4.57B vs $4.32B est, EBITDA $1.64B vs $1.36B est
bullets.body: Fox Corp reported Q1 records for both revenue and adjusted EBITDA, driven by FIFA Men's World Cup, college/NFL football, and election cycle advertising. EPS $2.54 ex-items vs. FactSet $2.08; Television EBITDA $934M vs. $704.6M estimate. Short interest at 24%; near-term options imply ~8.3% move; revenue has beaten consensus in 17 of past 20 quarters.

bullets.title: MSFT: $25B debt offering; Azure +48% YoY; safest AI play per Wolfe
bullets.body: Microsoft launched a $25B debt offering (424B2) Monday morning. Azure growth accelerated to +48% YoY in 3Q26, with management guiding 49–50% next quarter; MSFT beat 3Q EPS by 3.9pts vs. expectations. Wolfe's Manic Monthly calls MSFT the safest way to play AI, and UBS flags it as beating EPS by 18.3% vs. 14.4% expected. MSFT cloud gross margin 66%; combined hyperscaler backlog $2.48T.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Cloud +103% but Search slowed; euro bond filed; Golden Dome DoD talks
bullets.body: Google Cloud grew 103% YoY in 3Q26 (gaining 200bps share to 26%), but Search revenue slowed to ~12% vs. ~14% expected, and the stock suffered its worst single-day post-earnings decline ever (-12.5%). GOOGL is in early talks with the Defense Department on the $185B Golden Dome program for data security. Alphabet also filed a euro-denominated bond offering in seven tranches.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS +39% with $578B backlog; Phillip Capital upgrades to Buy, $330 PT
bullets.body: AWS grew 39.3% YoY in 3Q26 with management projecting 40%+ growth in 2027–2028; backlog grew 189% YoY to $578B. However, AMZN missed 3Q EPS expectations by 4.0pts. Phillip Capital upgraded to Buy (from Accumulate), raising PT to $330 from $320 citing AWS strength; Mizuho raised PT to $335.

bullets.title: AMD: Earnings Tuesday; Dec-Q guide likely conservative; AI GPU CY27 upside to $42-48B
bullets.body: AMD reports Tuesday after close (consensus $13.1B revenue). Vanda/Jefferies modeling Dec-Q guidance conservative at $16.5B vs. Street $16.3B given PC weakness. CY27 AI GPU revenue modeled at $42B with upside to $48B on 14k racks, though supply/infrastructure constraints may limit execution. JPM buyside sentiment on AMD at +3.

bullets.title: INTC: Down ~30% post-earnings; 2027 flagged as investment year
bullets.body: Intel guided 4Q revenue ~$2B below buyside expectations with a 6% sequential revenue decline vs. 4% growth expected, its worst day since 1974. Manufacturing constraints persist into 2027; PC demand destruction from higher memory prices and wafer/substrate shortages compound server-side challenges. Evercore and Jefferies are bullish on INTC for the agentic server CPU cycle despite near-term pain.

bullets.title: CHKP: Billings -5% YoY; Citi cuts PT to $130, KeyBank Sector Weight
bullets.body: Check Point 3Q billings fell 5% YoY to $636M (missed by ~$9M), product revenue declined 19% YoY (third consecutive quarter of intensifying weakness), and operating margins compressed for the fourth consecutive quarter. Citi cut PT to $130 from $152 implying -14.5% downside; management acknowledged recovery is 'taking longer than anticipated.' Both Mizuho (Neutral, $145 PT) and KeyBank (Sector Weight) see 4Q guide needing to come down.

bullets.title: DKNG: Maintain Outperform; 2027 profit inflection intact at 10x EV/EBITDA
bullets.body: OPCO and TMT desk both reduce 2026/2027 EBITDA estimates 9%/7% (to ~$497M/$1.08B) on higher Predictions customer acquisition costs, but maintain Outperform given the 2027 profit inflection story. DKNG trades at 10x Street 2027E EV/EBITDA; Q3 handle up ~11% QTD, GGR up ~6% YoY. FLUT faces a larger headwind — OPCO cuts PT to $110 from $120 as softer holds and limited consumer predictions strategy weigh.

bullets.title: RDDT: Down 29% on DAU miss; self-inflicted logged-in transition creates revenue risk
bullets.body: Reddit reported $895M revenue vs. ~$950M expected with a 900K decline in US DAUs. JPM calculates RDDT must increase logged-in DAUs by ~13M (+25%) and achieve a ~17% conversion rate of logged-out users to maintain revenue neutrality, as logged-in users monetize at 5–6x the rate ($45/year vs. $8/year). SG&A jumped 73% YTD and adj. EBITDA margins contracted 600bps in Q3. D.A. Davidson notes 3Q beat but self-inflicted issues continue.

bullets.title: T/VZ: Down 2-3% on SpaceX-Boost Mobile talks; AT&T still JPM's top telecom pick
bullets.body: SpaceX is in active talks to acquire Boost Mobile or access its network, sending AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile down 2–3% in pre-market. Verizon, T-Mobile, and AT&T all declined Musk's prior network-access requests. JPM nonetheless keeps AT&T as its top November telecom pick with a $31 Dec'27 PT (9.0x 2028E FCF), citing 350K converged adds in 3Q and a 42.8% fiber convergence rate.

bullets.title: APP: Downgraded to Neutral at Edgewater on share losses and algo issues
bullets.body: AppLovin was downgraded to Neutral by Edgewater Research citing share losses to Unity and algorithm problems since July. This follows a broader TMT de-risking week; no new PT provided in the note.

bullets.title: CART/DASH: JPM suspends CART rating on DASH conflict; CART 3Q momentum strong
bullets.body: JPM suspended its CART rating and PT (acting as DASH's M&A advisor). CART 3Q GTV growth accelerated to 15% YoY, advertising revenue surged 23% (well above 15–18% guidance), and EBITDA of $342M beat the high end of guidance. CART repurchased $230M in shares.

bullets.title: Semis sector: SOX down 19% from highs; JPM prefers AVGO, NVDA defensively
bullets.body: The SOX fell 7.2% on Friday and is down 19.1% from October highs, with INTC and PC-related stocks leading the decline. Investor concerns center on fixed-income capital availability for AI buildout, PE funding commitment, equity support, power availability, and chip warehousing costs. JPM's defensive semi picks are AVGO, NVDA (no more negative discovery value), KLAC, AAPL; hedge funds are underweight the AI complex for the first time since early 2023, with positioning primarily reflecting short covering rather than new longs.

bullets.title: BE/CEG/ENPH: Power utilities +10% in October on data center PPAs; ENPH -16%
bullets.body: The S&P 500 Utilities Index rose 10% in October vs. S&P 500 +0.9%, driven by nuclear and fuel-cell PPAs: CEG signed a 20-year 890 MW nuclear deal with Google, AEP announced a 960 MW nuclear JV with Amazon, and BKH jumped 17% on a $1.8B Google data center deal. Bloom Energy beat 3Q EPS ($0.94 vs. $0.69 est.) and raised FY guidance. In contrast, ENPH fell 16% on a 3Q EPS miss and weak Q4 residential solar guidance; FSLR cut guidance.

bullets.title: NET/SNAP/SHOP/BKNG/HUBS: Key earnings this week
bullets.body: Major upcoming reporters: SHOP (Tue pre-open, $3.75B rev est), AMD and ANET (Tue after close), BKNG (Tue, $9.55B), EXPE and HUBS and SNAP (Wed), LYV and NET (Thu after close, NET $736.8M), CHTR (Fri pre-open). Jefferies notes the average downside move on T+1 earnings is -8% vs. +7% upside — biggest downside skew in 12-year data — cautioning on position sizing into prints.
